title: A same-universe representative extension of a Zariski torsor
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $G$ be an abelian sheaf on its small Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site], and let $T$ be a $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor]. There exists a short exact sequence $0\to G\xrightarrow{\iota}E\xrightarrow{p}\mathbf Z_X\to0$ of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology] such that $T$ is isomorphic, equivariantly for the $G$ action, to the sheaf of local lifts of the global section $1$ through $p$. Here $X$, the values of $G$, and the values of $E$ are in the same universe $u$. No cohomology-class identity is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 02FQ (cohomology-lemma-torsors-h1), first construction by pushout of the free abelian sheaf; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02FQ

proof.text: Form the free abelian sheaf Z[T] by sheafifying sectionwise finite integer sums. Its augmentation sends every generator to 1 in the constant integer sheaf. It is locally surjective since T has local sections. If t0 is a local section of T, the augmentation kernel sends sum n_i[t_i], with sum n_i = 0, to sum n_i(t_i - t0) in G. Changing t0 does not change this value because the sum of coefficients is zero. This defines a natural additive map a from the kernel to G.

Push out the augmentation kernel inclusion along a. Concretely E is the sheaf quotient of G direct-sum Z[T] by the image of k mapped to (-a(k),k). In the abelian sheaf category this gives a short exact sequence 0 -> G -> E -> Z_X -> 0. Locally at t0, the quotient is G direct-sum Z with [t] represented by (t - t0,1); in particular the inclusion is injective, the augmentation is surjective, and its kernel is precisely G. Exactness is local and hence holds globally.

The natural map t mapped to [t] takes values in the fibre over one and satisfies [g + t]=[t]+g. On any open where t0 exists, each fibre section is uniquely [t0]+g, so this map is a bijection on the fibre there. These local equivariant bijections glue to an isomorphism of T with the torsor of lifts of one. All sectionwise free groups, direct sums and quotients have coefficient universe u; sheafification on a topological space preserves that universe. This also applies when X is empty or G is zero.
